extracted.intended_audience: licensors and licensees of 5G technology, patent/IP professionals, standards bodies, and corporate/legal teams involved in SEP licensing
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether patents declared to 5G standards (ETSI) are technically essential to 5G specifications via manual claim-to-specification mapping, stratified sampling, and scoring to inform licensing negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency around the true number of SEPs
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure fair competition and to foster continued advancements within the telecommunications sector, it is crucial to have transparency around the true number of Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) owned by each company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many companies declare patents as ‘essential’ but not all patents are truly essential; declarations alone are a poor measure of essential patent counts. The report acts as a benchmark to bring transparency to the true number of essential patent families and aids licensors and licensees in negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual technical review of declared patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual reviews conducted on raw patent data pulled from ETSI by our engineers and experts enable identification of patents that are truly essential to the technical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This manual review approach, together with a robust sampling method, differentiates this analysis from other 5G patent reports on the market and provides a more accurate picture of the SEP landscape and individual company SEP share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratified sample-based approach by declaring company
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the large number of patent families declared as potentially essential, an exhaustive analysis was not practical. A stratified sample-based approach was followed for the SEP essentiality patent ranking by performing technical reviews on each declaring company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring companies were split into groups based on the number of declared ETSI patent families (with at least one granted patent in US/EP/CN/KR/JP), and sampling/analysis was applied per group to produce representative essentiality estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: consider families with at least one grant in US/EP/CN/KR/JP
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis focused on ETSI families with at least one granted patent in the world’s five largest patent jurisdictions: US/EP/CN/KR/JP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Out of 108,638 unique ETSI disclosures up to 18 Oct 2023, 48,015 ETSI families had at least one grant in these jurisdictions; these families formed the core of the evaluated universe for granted-status analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essentiality assessment via claim-to-specification mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether any of the independent claims of the patent read onto normative parts of the 5G Technical Specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents were assessed by mapping independent claims to the normative sections of 5G technical specs; a patent is scored as technically essential when at least one independent claim was found to be essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent scoring scale (rank 1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each assessed patent, a rank from one to four was given, with one being potentially essential to the technical standards, and four being not relevant by domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each patent was scored according to this 1–4 scale as part of the essentiality analysis; the scale provides granular classification of technical relevance to the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for scoring consistency and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review processes were carried out to ensure consistency of scoring principles and accuracy of claims mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review helps validate that scoring and claim-to-specification mappings are consistent across reviewers and that essentiality determinations are robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify inventions disclosed to ETSI and evaluate for technical essentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The team identified inventions as disclosed to ETSI and evaluated them for technical essentiality by mining patents declared to 5G relevant specifications and projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This involves mining the declaration data, extracting the disclosed inventions/families, and assessing claim coverage against the relevant 5G specification elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for declared families vs granted patents/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that many declared patents are applications that have not been granted; uncertainty in grant outcomes means the actual number of granted patents can be significantly lower than the declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports separate declared families with a 5G grant in US/EP/CN/KR/JP from declared families without granted members in those jurisdictions; this distinction is important when estimating the current universe of granted 5G patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and use essentiality percentage and portfolio-level comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate essentiality percentage per portfolio/patent holder to compare true essential patent counts across owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios with many declared patents but a low essentiality percentage may contain fewer essential patents than smaller portfolios with a higher essentiality percentage. Essentiality percentage has changed over time and varies between owners; use percentage rather than raw declaration counts to benchmark portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map patent portfolios to technology features and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Map assessed patent portfolios to specific technology features and parts of the standards to provide detailed profiling of each holder’s strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full report provides mapping of portfolios to technology features and standards and the full database of patent reviews, enabling transparent views of essentiality and aiding licensing negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ETSI disclosures/raw patent data as primary data source
rubrics_metrics.description: Base analysis on raw patent declaration data pulled from ETSI as the authoritative source of declared potentially-essential patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw ETSI data is mined for declarations relevant to 5G specifications/projects; reliance on ETSI disclosures underpins the sampling and manual review pipeline.
